symbols.description: Latin capital C (open to the right)
open (outline) triangle, apex up; same shape as the Z408/Z340 hollow triangle
capital J with a short top bar
plain vertical stroke (sans-serif capital I, no serifs); matches the Z340 'bar' symbol, not the serifed Z408 I
capital O (open oval/circle, no inner mark)

inverted-T-like glyph: a vertical stem standing on a short base whose right end curls upward into a hook; the left end is rounded and slightly upturned (a perpendicular sign with hooked feet). Oranchak's Cipher Explorer names it 't2', a variant kept distinct from the plain Z408/Z340 perpendicular 't'; the same glyph occurs in Z13
Greek capital omega (horseshoe-shaped arch with two feet); occurs in no other Zodiac cipher
capital G drawn with an inward curl (resembles a 6); same glyph as the Z408/Z340 G
circle with a solid dot at its centre
mirror-reversed J: horizontal top bar (small downward tick at its left end) with a stem from about mid-bar that curves to the right at the bottom; resembles Greek tau
outlined square with its lower-right diagonal half filled (small open triangle remains at upper left)
Zodiac crosshair: circle with a cross whose arms extend beyond the circle (the Zodiac's signature symbol)

uncertainties: Position 3 ('|'): drawn as a plain vertical stroke without serifs. The convention transcribes it as the Z340 bar '|' (Z340 key: E). Some treat the Z340 bar and the serifed Z408 'I' as one symbol (the zodiackillerciphers.com wiki alphabet comparison notes this option); if equated, the Z408 key would give T. AZdecrypt's bundled 'Zodiac 32 with 408 key.txt' instead decodes this position as E, which matches no Z408 symbol under the ASCII convention (unexplained).

Position 3: the SFPD photograph (zodiackillerciphers.com wiki 'Button Letter with 32 code large.jpg') shows a tiny grey ring just below the stroke, making it look like '!'. It is absent from the color scan (Commons/zodiackiller.com) and looks like a paper or photo defect, not ink; we do not treat it as part of the symbol.

Position 7 ('['): inverted T whose base hooks upward at the right end; the left end is rounded and slightly upturned. Transcribed as a distinct symbol ('t2' in Oranchak's Cipher Explorer, '[' in AZdecrypt) absent from Z408/Z340. Alternative: treat it as a variant of the plain perpendicular 't' (Z408 R, Z340 L). AZdecrypt's 'Zodiac 32 with 408 key.txt' decodes it as O, i.e. it apparently equates it with a Z408 symbol that decodes to O (perhaps the curled 'funny I' '!'); this is undocumented.
Position 12 ('?'): Greek capital omega; no counterpart in Z408 or Z340 ('?' is the character AZdecrypt and Cipher Explorer use for it; Cipher Explorer names it 'omega').

Position 22 ('j'): mirror-reversed J with top bar, which also looks like Greek tau or a rotated 2. The convention equates it with the Z408/Z340 backwards-J (Z408 X, Z340 P), which looks the same in Oranchak's symbol images.

Position 23 ('%'): we confirmed the orientation on the color scan: lower-right half filled, open triangle at upper left. That is the same orientation as the Z340 '%' (row 2, column 8 of the Z340 scan) and as the half-filled square that Oranchak's combined Z408/Z340 key image lists with Z408 L / Z340 T. AZdecrypt's 'Zodiac 32 with 408 key.txt' nevertheless treats this symbol as absent from Z408 (unexplained).

Position 11 ('8', filled triangle): in Z408 the as-enciphered key (AZdecrypt) decodes it as A everywhere, but the Hardens' reading interprets several occurrences as S (MOST rather than MOAT), so its Z408 value is A (or S).

Positions 1 and 31 ('9', open triangle) vs position 11 ('8', filled triangle): they are clearly different (outline vs solid) in every scan. At least one 2026 analysis (Praetorian blog) counted all three as one 'TRIANGLE' symbol; we keep them distinct, as all transcriptions in the convention do.

Positions 0/25 ('C') and 5/13 ('O'): the two instances of each differ slightly in size and roundness, but every source treats them as the same symbol. These three pairs (with 1/31) are the only repeats; 29 distinct symbols in 32.
Layout: 17 symbols on line 1 and 15 on line 2, both starting at the left margin. Reading order is assumed to be left to right, top line first; no transposition is known.

notes: Unsolved. No plaintext or key is accepted. The fields 'plaintext', 'key' and 'read_order' are therefore omitted.

Repeats: C at 0 and 25, open triangle '9' at 1 and 31, O at 5 and 13 (0-based). 29 distinct symbols in 32 (multiplicity 29/32 = 0.91). Under a homophonic substitution, a plaintext must satisfy p[0]=p[25], p[1]=p[31], p[5]=p[13]; no other constraint follows from the ciphertext alone.
Isomorph letters are assigned a-z, then A-Z, then 0-9 in order of first appearance.

Key carry-over (Z408 letter, Z340 letter; '-' = symbol absent), from the AZdecrypt Z408/Z340 ciphertext and solution files: C: Z408 -, Z340 Y; 9: Z408 I, Z340 N; J: Z408 F, Z340 S; |: Z408 -, Z340 E; #: Z408 L, Z340 T; O: Z408 N, Z340 A; k: Z408 I, Z340 I; [: Z408 -, Z340 -; A: Z408 W, Z340 D; M: Z408 H, Z340 O; f: Z408 D, Z340 B; 8: Z408 A, Z340 P; ?: Z408 -, Z340 -; R: Z408 G, Z340 O; T: Z408 O, Z340 R; G: Z408 A, Z340 T; X: Z408 O, Z340 R; 6: Z408 E, Z340 D; F: Z408 S, Z340 F; D: Z408 N, Z340 N; V: Z408 B, Z340 O; j: Z408 X, Z340 P; %: Z408 L, Z340 T; H: Z408 T, Z340 I; E: Z408 E, Z340 R; L: Z408 T, Z340 G; z: Z408 D, Z340 A; P: Z408 I, Z340 I; W: Z408 E, Z340 W.
Z32 under the Z408 key (strict ASCII identity): ?IF?LNI?WHDA?NGOA / OESNBXLT?ETDIEI. If the bar '|' is equated with Z408 'I' and '[' with Z408 't': ?IFTLNIRWHDA?NGOA / OESNBXLT?ETDIEI.
Z32 under the Z340 key (strict ASCII identity): YNSETAI?DOBP?AORT / RDFNOPTIYRGAIWN. If '[' is equated with Z340 't': YNSETAILDOBP?AORT / RDFNOPTIYRGAIWN.

Neither carried-over key yields readable English. AZdecrypt ships the same two decodes as 'Zodiac 32 with 340 key.txt' (identical to ours) and 'Zodiac 32 with 408 key.txt' (differs from ours at positions 3, 7 and 23; see uncertainties).

Context: the letter was postmarked 1970-06-26 in San Francisco and addressed to the S.F. Chronicle. It came with a cut-out Phillips 66 road map inset ('San Francisco and Vicinity'), marked with a Zodiac crosshair on Mt. Diablo, numbered 0/3/6/9 clockwise from the top, and labelled '0 is to be set to Mag. N.'. The 1970-07-26 'Little List' letter adds a postscript tying the Mt. Diablo code to radians and inches along the radians. See research/z32_literature.md and research/z32_map.md.

The color scan on Commons (Zodiac-Colour-SFC.jpg) is byte-identical to zodiackiller.com images/phillips66letter.jpg, so it is not an independent image. The SFPD photograph and the zodiackiller.com black-and-white scan are separate images, and all three agree on every symbol.

checked_against_images: data/images/z32_cipher_clean_commons.png (Commons redrawing; used only as a cross-check)
findings: All three independent images show 17 symbols on row 1 and 15 on row 2, identical to the ascii string glyph for glyph.
Position 3 is a plain stroke without serifs: '|' (Z340 bar), not the serifed Z408 'I'.
Position 7 is the hooked inverted T, the same glyph as Z13 position 9 ('['); Z340's 't' is drawn without the hook.

Position 22 is the backwards J drawn like a tau (top bar with a small tick at the left end, stem curling right). The two Z340 'j' glyphs (0-based rows 4 and 7 of the Commons Z340 colour photo, https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:4abc_-_San_Francisco_Chronicle_Dripping_Pen_Card_November_8_1969_340_Cipher_COLOR.jpg) are drawn the same way, and Oranchak's combined key image (http://zodiackillerciphers.com/images/z408-z340-combined-keys.png) shows this shape for Z408 X / Z340 P, so 'j' is kept.

Position 23 is a square filled except for an open triangle at the upper left. Z340 has both orientations in one row (0-based row 1 of the same photo: '%' at column 7 is open at the upper left, '*' at column 13 is open at the upper right); the Z32 glyph matches '%', which the combined key image lists as Z408 L / Z340 T.
Positions 1 and 31 are open triangles ('9'); position 11 is a solid triangle ('8'). Position 12 is an omega ('?'), found in no other cipher.
Derived fields (isomorph, counts, positions, in_z13/in_z408/in_z340) recomputed from ascii by tools/certify_ciphers.py; the only change was the new in_z13 flag.

transcription_variants.basis: Oranchak wiki, AZdecrypt Zodiac 32.txt and Cipher Explorer zodiac.js; confirmed on three independent images (see certification).

transcription_variants.change: position 3: '|' -> 'I' (serifed Z408 I, Z408 key T)
transcription_variants.basis: The glyph has no serifs, but the convention notes that the bar and the serifed I may be one symbol written two ways.

transcription_variants.change: position 7: '[' -> 't' (Z408 key R, Z340 key L)
transcription_variants.basis: Same question as Z13 position 9; the hook distinguishes the glyph as drawn.
Maximises the overlap with the Z408 key (only C and the omega stay unmatched).

transcription_variants.change: position 11: solid triangle '8' -> open triangle '9' (one triangle symbol at 1, 11, 31)
transcription_variants.basis: Praetorian blog (2026) counts all three as one triangle. Every image shows position 11 solid and 1/31 outlined, and Z408/Z340 treat solid and open triangles as different symbols.

transcription_variants.change: position 22: 'j' -> '$' (a separate tau-like symbol; '$' is the code Oranchak's webtoy reserves, commented out, for a 'tao' glyph)
transcription_variants.basis: Only matters for key carry-over (Z408 X, Z340 P); inside Z32 the symbol occurs once either way.
